identity.description: The generic parametric AFT alternatives to Weibull, covered by ONE driver with a `distribution` hyperparameter. Covariates rescale survival TIME (time-ratio reading, like weibull_aft) but the assumed lifetime distribution admits NON-monotone hazards — the hump-shaped/unimodal hazards Weibull cannot express. Neither distribution satisfies proportional hazards (log-logistic satisfies proportional ODDS instead), so this is the AFT-only branch of the family.

consumes.note: the (duration, event-indicator) pair carried as two columns alongside the covariate matrix

emits.note: closed-form S(t|x) under the chosen distribution — smooth and defined beyond the observed window
closed-form absolute h(t|x); log-normal/log-logistic hazards can RISE THEN FALL — the shape regime that justifies this sheet over weibull_aft
log time-ratios with CIs: exp(coef) is an acceleration factor on survival time — NOT a hazard ratio; there is no PH reading here at all
predicted median/expected survival time per row

distribution.note: the family driver dispatches LogNormalAFTFitter vs LogLogisticAFTFitter on this — a genuine model-selection hyperparameter; select by AIC on the shared full-likelihood scale, NOT by C-index (ranking barely distinguishes them)

penalizer.note: elastic-net strength on the regression coefficients

ancillary.note: when true, the ancillary (scale/shape) parameter is also regressed on covariates — covariates change dispersion, not just location

invariances.why: log(T) is modeled linearly in covariates; coefficients are per-unit log time-ratios — unscaled features give incomparable magnitudes and unstable optimization
the log-linear location form means a monotone covariate transform changes the fit
the parametric likelihood has no missing-value handling — NaN covariate rows are dropped or must be imputed

assumes the FULL lifetime distribution chosen by the `distribution` HP. Mechanism contrast with the rest of the family: AFT means covariates act multiplicatively on TIME — S(t|x)=S0(t*exp(-x'b)) — whereas PH (Cox) means they act multiplicatively on HAZARD. Log-normal and log-logistic admit non-monotone (hump-shaped) hazards and do NOT satisfy PH — log-logistic satisfies proportional odds — so their fitted rankings can legitimately disagree with Cox when hazards cross
the full parametric likelihood extracts more per event than a partial likelihood — usable at low event counts IF the chosen distribution holds
the closed parametric form extends S(t|x) beyond the last observed time — the payoff for the distributional assumption

featureStats.why: THE commit-survival stat: the right-censored fraction is what makes a survival model necessary vs a fixed-window classifier
effective sample size is the number of events; few events flags a penalizer and wide CIs

the empirical hazard shape (smoothed Nelson-Aalen from the KM baseline) is the router WITHIN the parametric branch: monotone supports Weibull, hump-shaped/unimodal supports log-normal or log-logistic — the math these distributions differ on

modelMetrics.why: the survival-native ranking metric (Harrell's C) — with the ceiling caveat: near-deterministic durations inflate C toward 1, so it is reported with the censoring context, never alone
the shared full-likelihood scale makes AIC the honest selector for the `distribution` hyperparameter (and vs weibull_aft) — a within-family comparison C-index cannot make

edgeCases.behavior: likelihood carries no event information — parameters unidentifiable
both distributions have support strictly t > 0; log(t) undefined — fit raises

edgeCases.condition: chosen distribution misfits the empirical hazard shape
edgeCases.behavior: systematically biased curves and time-ratios despite convergence
edgeCases.note: compare AIC across {weibull, lognormal, loglogistic}; persistent misfit across all three routes to RSF

edgeCases.behavior: coefficient diverges, optimizer fails to converge

driver.constructor: {LogNormalAFTFitter|LogLogisticAFTFitter}(penalizer=..., l1_ratio=...).fit(df, duration_col, event_col, ancillary=...) — class dispatched on the `distribution` hyperparameter
driver.wrapperNeeds: adapter: (duration,event) columns split from the matrix; a small dispatch map {lognormal: LogNormalAFTFitter, loglogistic: LogLogisticAFTFitter}; predict maps to predict_survival_function / predict_median / predict_hazard

placementClaims.why: no native NaN handling; unimputed rows are silently dropped, biasing the likelihood
log/Yeo-Johnson of skewed covariates improves the log-linear location fit
coefficients are per-unit log time-ratios; standardization makes acceleration factors comparable and optimization stable
categoricals must be design-encoded before entering the parametric likelihood
